Observations have been performed with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) towards the sample of IRDCs described in Barnes et al. in prep. (hereafter paper I). The project IDs are 2017.1.00687.S and 2018.1.00850.S (PI: A.T. Barnes).
In this paper, we present the first interferometric study of the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio towards a large sample of IRDC cores in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ at high-angular resolution.

In particular, because each core is classified as starless or star-forming within each cloud, we are also able to compare the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios with the presence/absence of protostellar activity.

all_quotes.quote: when the line profile was attributed more likely to self-absorption (e.g. in the cores D6c6, D7c1 and D7c2), we have integrated the whole component, bearing in mind that this will provide a lower limit on $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$), and hence a lower limit on the associated $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N as well.

Another caveat on the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios arises from the possible non negligible optical depth of the F$_1=0-1$ component of N$_{2}$H$^{+}$(1–0), which could lead us to underestimate $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$) and, from this, the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio.

A few of them are indeed associated, but unfortunately only 4 of those are also detected in N$^{15}$NH$^+$, and thus the statistics is too low to discuss possible relations between nitrogen and deuterium fractionation.

In fact, first the nature of our starless cores could not be "pre–stellar" but just starless or star-forming in a very early stage of star-formation activity; second, some cores are extended and could contain smaller fragments in different evolutionary stages.

However, all trends are strongly influenced by sources F1c1 and F1c2 (Figs. 6 and 7). Moreover, most N$^{15}$NH$^+$ lines are detected with a signal to noise ratio in between 3 and 5, and hence any trend that can be found from the plots in Figs. 6 and 7 must be taken with caution.

However, the temperature of our cores at the scales studied by us is always above $\sim 10$ K, in agreement with the lack of $^{15}$N enrichment, although the temperature measurement is taken over an angular scale (i.e. the Herschel beam) larger than that of the individual cores.
